title: Biobank for blood samples and biomaterials samples of patients with spinal diseases
summary:
Despite state-of-the-art therapies, there is still a risk of infection of the intervertebral disc space and vertebral bodies. However, many other spinal disorders, e.g. agerelated changes or osteoporotic fractures, also significantly impair quality of life. In order to prevent infections and develop more targeted treatments for patients, it is necessary to better understand the nature of the pathogen and the effect of antibiotics.  
The aim is to build up a collection of tissue samples (intraoperative biomaterial, e.g., from the intervertebral disc) and corresponding blood samples over a period of 10-20 years and to examine them in relation to various microbiological and immunological questions
conditions: Degeneration of the spine (e.g., herniated disc, spinal canal stenosis, spondylolisthesis), vertebral infection (e.g., spondylitis, spondylodiscitis, facet joint arthritis), and osteoporotic vertebral/pelvic fracture.

interventions.name:
Patients with (suspected) underlying degeneration of the spine (e.g., herniated disc, spinal canal stenosis, spondylolisthesis), vertebral infection (e.g., spondylitis, spondylodiscitis, facet joint arthritis), and osteoporotic vertebral/pelvic fracture requiring surgical treatment.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Suspicion of a degenerative, inflammatory disease or osteoporotic fracture of the spine or pelvic skeleton
• The patient is able to understand the nature, significance, and implications of the decision to participate in the study and to act in accordance with their wishes. 
• A declaration of consent dated and signed by the patient is available.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of consent to participate in the study
